catalog_quote: [2.3.1, pp.4-5] High tone has three allotones, conditioned by its occurrence with stress, or its occurrence on unstressed syllables. Stress occurs on the final high tone of a word, and in the absence of a high, it occurs on the final low. ... [3. WORD, p.5] The phonological word is composed of one or more syllables. Each word carries only one primary stress, the placement of which is determined by the tone pattern of the word as described in section 2.3.1. Thus stress occurs on the final syllable of ... onibá 'snake', ..., on the medial syllable of síbági 'sweet potato type', gomági 'type of sweet potato', and the first syllable of ákola 'wild fig tree'. The borders of the phonological word may be determined by potential pause, and stress placement. ... [note 7, p.7] There is contrastive stress on words with the tone pattern ´´`. audit.recode_to: No recode. Keep kind='weight' (tone-driven), edge='unbounded' (stress on rightmost H-toned syllable, else final syllable; compounds stress first H, note 7). Add to contra/caution: Evans & Stoakes 2005 (Materials on Golin pp.3-29) reanalyse a neighbouring sub-variety (speaker Chris Kia Aina) as three-way WORD tone (H/M/L) with the tone-defining pitch target on the last mora of the domain, reject the Bunns' two-way syllable-tone premise for that variety, and posit no word stress; they call the account preliminary and state (p.26) they 'cannot be certain whether the variety described by the Bunns would yield to reanalysis'.

sources.quote: p.3: 'On the analysis we present here, Golin is a word-tone language with three contrasting tones - high, mid and low - associated at the level of the word (or perhaps the foot). Tones are attached to the rightmost mora of their domain, with a relatively constant pitch realization at that point, but more freedom in the rest of the domain'. p.7: 'This analysis differs doubly from those published by the Bunns: we recognize an additional tone (medium) ... and on their analysis each syllable has one toneme, high or low (Bunn & Bunn 1970:4), whereas for us the toneme is associated with a higher-lev

sources.note: Only instrumentally informed (F0/Praat) prosodic analysis of Golin; reanalyses the Bunns' two-tone syllable-tone system (the premise of our 'stress on final H' rule) as three-way word tone anchored to the final mora and posits no stress. fetched sources now.
